Bootstrap confidence interval for a scalar statistic

Source: R/boot_ci.r
ks_boot_ci.Rd

Convenience wrapper around boot: resamples, computes a user statistic, and returns a percentile (BCa when defined) confidence interval plus the point estimate — one line instead of the usual `boot()` / `boot.ci()` plumbing in report code.

Usage

ks_boot_ci(
  x,
  statistic,
  R = 2000L,
  conf = 0.95,
  seed = NULL,
  type = c("perc", "basic", "norm", "bca")
)

Arguments

x

Data resampled by row: a vector, matrix, or data frame.

statistic

Function with signature `function(data, indices)` returning a **single numeric value** (scalar). `indices` select rows of `x`.

R

Number of bootstrap replicates (default `2000`).

conf

Confidence level (default `0.95`).

seed

Integer seed for reproducibility (default `NULL`).

type

Interval type: `"perc"` (percentile, default), `"basic"`, `"norm"`, or `"bca"`.

Value

A list with `estimate`, `std.error`, `lcl`, `ucl`, `type`, `conf.level`, the full `boot.ci` list in `$ci`, and the raw `boot` object in `$replicates`.

Details

The statistic must be scalar-valued; `ks_boot_ci()` checks the shape of the replicate matrix and aborts otherwise. BCa can be undefined (e.g. degenerate statistics on small samples) — the function then falls back to the percentile interval with a warning.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- rnorm(50, 5, 2)
ks_boot_ci(x, function(d, i) mean(d[i]))
#> $estimate
#> [1] 5.200897
#> 
#> $std.error
#> [1] 0.2339554
#> 
#> $lcl
#> [1] 4.733967
#> 
#> $ucl
#> [1] 5.664849
#> 
#> $type
#> [1] "perc"
#> 
#> $conf.level
#> [1] 0.95
#> 
#> $ci
#> BOOTSTRAP CONFIDENCE INTERVAL CALCULATIONS
#> Based on 2000 bootstrap replicates
#> 
#> CALL : 
#> boot::boot.ci(boot.out = b, conf = conf, type = c("perc", "bca", 
#>     "basic", "norm"))
#> 
#> Intervals : 
#> Level      Normal              Basic         
#> 95%   ( 4.733,  5.651 )   ( 4.737,  5.668 )  
#> 
#> Level     Percentile            BCa          
#> 95%   ( 4.734,  5.665 )   ( 4.654,  5.594 )  
#> Calculations and Intervals on Original Scale
#> 
#> $replicates
#> 
#> ORDINARY NONPARAMETRIC BOOTSTRAP
#> 
#> 
#> Call:
#> boot::boot(data = x, statistic = statistic, R = as.integer(R))
#> 
#> 
#> Bootstrap Statistics :
#>     original      bias    std. error
#> t1* 5.200897 0.008936649   0.2339554
#> 

# ratio of two columns (paired resampling)
d <- data.frame(a = rnorm(60, 5, 1), b = rnorm(60, 3, 1))
ks_boot_ci(d, function(dd, i) mean(dd$a[i]) / mean(dd$b[i]), R = 999,
           seed = 42)
#> $estimate
#> [1] 1.521055
#> 
#> $std.error
#> [1] 0.07443549
#> 
#> $lcl
#> [1] 1.383033
#> 
#> $ucl
#> [1] 1.672262
#> 
#> $type
#> [1] "perc"
#> 
#> $conf.level
#> [1] 0.95
#> 
#> $ci
#> BOOTSTRAP CONFIDENCE INTERVAL CALCULATIONS
#> Based on 999 bootstrap replicates
#> 
#> CALL : 
#> boot::boot.ci(boot.out = b, conf = conf, type = c("perc", "bca", 
#>     "basic", "norm"))
#> 
#> Intervals : 
#> Level      Normal              Basic         
#> 95%   ( 1.373,  1.665 )   ( 1.370,  1.659 )  
#> 
#> Level     Percentile            BCa          
#> 95%   ( 1.383,  1.672 )   ( 1.383,  1.672 )  
#> Calculations and Intervals on Original Scale
#> 
#> $replicates
#> 
#> ORDINARY NONPARAMETRIC BOOTSTRAP
#> 
#> 
#> Call:
#> boot::boot(data = x, statistic = statistic, R = as.integer(R))
#> 
#> 
#> Bootstrap Statistics :
#>     original      bias    std. error
#> t1* 1.521055 0.002006082  0.07443549
#>
